minutes.headline: Sewer Commission agreed to buy spare pump parts and start I&I Task 1; contested minutes were tabled.
minutes.summary: The commission signed a settlement agreement, then reviewed Small Water's list of spare pump station parts and agreed to buy it while keeping a reserve for emergencies. It took up I&I Task 1, a maintenance and capital plan, the Tilton extension notice, the FY19 budget and the Fitchburg rate proposal. A long dispute over edited minutes ended with the minutes tabled. A resident raised open meeting law concerns in public comment.

public_comment.topic: Alleged open meeting law violations: communications passed through a staff member and late minutes; urged minutes approval at start of meetings.

budget_items.what_was_said: Budget status of the purchase of service section was reviewed against Task 1, John Street repairs, Highfield village counsel and the spare parts list.
Members worked out how much would remain for emergencies after buying the parts and holding money for I&I.
The project came in under budget so the annual debt payment was reduced.
An invoice matching the flow meter and the third quarter bill commitment were reported.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to buy the spare pump station parts on Small Water's list and move money out of I&I so more is held for emergencies.
It voted to accept the Task 1 report as written and begin work on I&I Task 1; the vote tally was not audible.
The commission tabled the minutes after a long dispute over edits, and agreed to move minutes approval to the start of future meetings.
Members agreed by consensus on edits to the Tilton extension letter, with a response deadline of March 13.
The business manager will research a pump station engineering study, and Jack will talk with Small Water about maintenance.

why_it_matters: Spare parts and the I&I work are paid from sewer purchase-of-service money, so these choices affect how much is left for emergency repairs and, over time, what sewer users are charged.
Moving minutes approval to the start of meetings changes when the public can see a settled record of what the commission decided.
watch_next: March 13, the response deadline set for the Tilton extension letter.
Approval of the tabled minutes, now to be taken at the start of future meetings.
